stories.title: Kishtwar terror attack case: NIA files chargesheet
stories.summary: Jammu, Oct 9: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Friday filed a chargesheet before the NIA Special Court Jammu against an arrested accused and three killed Pakistani terrorists in the Kishtwar terror attack case. In a statement, NIA said it filed the 535-page chargesheet against arrested accused Maneer Ahmed, son of Mohammad Yousuf Koli, resident of Naidgam Chatroo, Inderwal, Kishtwar and three killed terrorists including Saifullah @ Saifullah Kashmiri @ Atiq Nazir @ Atiq Ur Rehman. The chargesheet pertains to the terror attack on 22nd February 2026 at Chatroo, Wani Mohalla, Passer Kote in Kishtwar (RC-03/2026/NIA/JMU). The chargesheet details the conspiracy, the role of the three killed terrorists including Saifullah, a resident of Pakistan and commander of proscribed outfit Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM), and of arrested accused Maneer Ahmed, along with supporting evidence. It charges Maneer Ahmed with voluntarily harbouring and concealing terrorists involved in attacks on security forces and civilians in hilly district Kishtwar under relevant provisions of UA(P) Act, 1967. NIA has also invoked penal section against the accused terrorists for waging war against India and hatching conspiracy from across the border. As per NIA, the attack involved three terrorists led by terror commander Saifullah, affiliated to Kashmir Tigers (Azrael Group), which acts under the proscribed outfit JeM. Retaliatory fire from security forces led to killing of all three. The group, which was active in upper reaches of Kishtwar, was found to have conducted several attacks that resulted in killing of security forces personnel and locals. Arrested accused Maneer Ahmed has been found to be involved in providing support to the group. NIA’s investigation, spanning almost 5 months, has traced the conspiracy to Pakistan. Further investigation in the case is continuing, the agency in a statement said.

A public interest litigation has been filed before the Supreme Court seeking directions to declare the Baiga-dominated Birsa and Baihar blocks of Madhya Pradesh's Balaghat district an epidemic-prone area under the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897, following deaths of over 30 tribal children due to measles-rubella and severe malnutrition.

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana today issued notice to the Union, the State, NHRC and other official respondents on the plea after hearing Advocate Varun Thakur for the petitioner.

The petition alleges that administrative negligence, inadequate healthcare facilities, malnutrition and a failure to ensure timely immunisation contributed to the deaths of children in remote tribal settlements.
It seeks compensation for affected families, the provision of safe drinking water and nutritious food, and implementation of government welfare schemes for the tribal community.

“Despite robust statutory frameworks specifically designed to protect their habitat and existence, the State apparatus has manifested a colossal systemic failure, allowing a treatable viral infection to decimate an already fragile population.

Despite explicit, written warnings submitted to the district administration and public representatives as early as January 2026, the State apparatus remained in a bureaucratic slumber”, the plea states.
More than 35 children belonging to the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) have reportedly died in the affected areas following an outbreak of measles-rubella and severe malnutrition.
The petition alleges that the administration failed to undertake adequate disease surveillance, provide essential medicines and deploy medical teams despite being alerted to the situation.

The petition also challenges an order issued by the Additional District Magistrate of Balaghat on September 3 under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 prohibiting citizens, journalists and healthcare workers from photographing, recording videos or reels, or publishing information about conditions inside public offices and health facilities on social media.
The petition contends that the restriction is meant to suppress evidence of administrative failures and infringes the constitutional right to freedom of speech and expression.
Notably, the Balaghat administration withdrew the September 3 order within hours of issuing it, stating that it had been issued in haste and was not intended to prevent media coverage.

stories.headline: Leading dentists redefining modern dentistry through innovation, impact and excellence
stories.title: Leading dentists redefining modern dentistry through innovation, impact and excellence
stories.summary: Dentistry today extends far beyond traditional clinical care. From advanced implantology and digital orthodontics to cosmetic dentistry, preventive healthcare, and dental education, a new generation of practitioners is reshaping how oral healthcare is delivered and understood.These dentists come from diverse backgrounds and bring different areas of expertise, but they share a common focus on combining clinical knowledge with innovation, patient care, education, and meaningful impact. Their work reflects the evolving face of dentistry, where technology, entrepreneurship, sustainability, and community service are increasingly becoming part of the profession.Dr. Arumalla Sridhar Reddy: Transforming Lives Through Dentistry and Community Service Dr. Arumalla Sridhar Reddy, an Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon, has made community healthcare a significant part of his professional journey. He has provided free dental health checkups to more than 1.2 million schoolchildren across underserved communities and holds a Guinness World Record for conducting the world’s largest dental health checkup, covering 21,233 students within eight hours.His contributions extend beyond dental care, with Dr. Reddy supporting three orphanage homes that provide care, education, and healthcare to around 250 children.He has also facilitated thousands of free orthognathic surgeries for underprivileged patients and has reportedly received the President of India’s Gold Medal twice for contributions to social service and community welfare.Dr. Shilfa Nigar: Innovating Sustainable DentistryDr. Shilfa Nigar is a practising cosmetic dentist and entrepreneur, building her next chapter around Ecoligners, a dental venture focused on making eco-friendly aligner treatment more accessible and sustainability-conscious. The venture aims to address the waste associated with disposable clear aligners by exploring recyclable solutions and bringing an environmental perspective to modern orthodontic treatment.With nearly a decade of clinical experience, Dr. Shilfa has also been recognised as India’s first General Dental Practitioner to achieve Black Diamond Invisalign Provider status. Beyond dentistry, she has created work-from-home opportunities for around 100 female dentists, enabling them to continue working outside conventional clinical practice.Her journey reflects the intersection of clinical expertise, entrepreneurship, sustainability and social impact.Dr. M. Vijaya Lakshmi Macherla: Crafting Personalised SmilesDr. M. Vijaya Lakshmi Macherla is a dental surgeon, implantologist, and smile designing specialist with 28 years of experience. A first-generation doctor, she began her practice in 2009 with a single dental chair and has since expanded it to three branches in Hyderabad, with a team of doctors and predominantly female staff. Her work in smile designing focuses on creating natural-looking, personalised smiles based on each patient’s facial features, dental needs, and expectations.Beyond clinical practice, Dr. Vijaya Lakshmi has focused on continuous learning with predominantly women-led clinical and support staff. She has also built a social media community of over 3 lakh people, where she shares dental awareness and practical health tips. She has conducted dental camps in government schools and supported free consultations for orphans and physically challenged individuals, along with treatment concessions through social initiatives.Her professional journey also includes advanced training and exposure to international dental programmes, veneers, and digital dentistry, alongside recognition for her contributions to the field.Dr. Prathamesh Kshatriya: Building a New Age Healthcare EcosystemDr. Prathamesh Kshatriya, an oral implantologist and healthcare entrepreneur, has spent nearly eight years studying content, marketing and the psychology behind what makes people pay attention. That experience led him to build Vantage & Cole, a healthcare-focused growth company working with doctors, clinics, hospitals and healthcare brands across positioning, communication, digital growth and market strategy.Kshatriya has also worked behind the scenes as a consultant and growth advisor to healthcare businesses, helping shape how they communicate, position themselves and connect with their audiences. Known for a storytelling style that often gives language to what doctors and students are already thinking or feeling, he has developed a distinctive presence within the healthcare community.Alongside this, he has built Doctors Coach into a community of more than 2 Lakh doctors, dentists and healthcare students, with conversations spanning money, artificial intelligence, entrepreneurship and emerging career opportunities. His work today brings together healthcare, storytelling, media and business.Dr. Prajakta Nawgiri: Transforming Smiles Through Modern DentistryDr. Prajakta Nawgiri is a Cosmetic and Paediatric Dentist and the Founder and Chief Dentist of VISTA Dental, Pune, an award-winning multispeciality dental practice. With over 12 years of experience across Mumbai and Pune, including five years in corporate dentistry, she has treated more than 8,000 patients and built VISTA Dental around clinical excellence, aesthetics and a patient-centric approach.Specialising in cosmetic dentistry and smile designing, Dr. Prajakta focuses on personalised and natural-looking smile transformations. Her practice integrates digital dentistry and advanced dental technology into diagnosis, treatment planning and patient care. Her clientele includes celebrities, entrepreneurs and professionals, with patients travelling from across India and internationally for treatment. A recipient of two FAMDENT Excellence in Dentistry Awards, her journey brings together clinical practice, entrepreneurship and the evolution of a modern, technology-driven dental practice.Dr. Kavita Bhat Kumar: 30 Years of Transforming SmilesDr. Kavita Bhat Kumar is a cosmetic dentist and founder of Designer Smiles, a multispeciality dental clinic in Vile Parle East, Mumbai, which she has led since 1995. With over 30 years of clinical experience, she has built her practice around smile makeovers and aesthetic dentistry, focusing on personalised, natural-looking and conservative treatment. Over the years, her practice has attracted clientele including professionals, models, public figures and patients travelling from overseas for dental care. Her training includes advanced aesthetic dentistry in Germany and specialised education in soft and hard tissue lasers at the University of Bonn.Her approach combines technology with clinical judgement, while giving equal importance to patient comfort and the overall treatment experience. As an Invisalign provider, she incorporates clear aligner therapy into selected cases. Under her leadership, Designer Smiles received the FAMDENT Excellence in Dentistry Award for Clinic of the Year in 2021. She is also a member of the Indian Academy of Aesthetic & Cosmetic Dentistry.Dr. Rachita Guru: Making Dental Education Digital Dr. Rachita Guru is an MDS Orthodontist, Gold Medallist and Invisalign Provider who practises across Gurgaon, Lucknow and Sonipat. She specialises in digital orthodontics, clear aligner therapy and aesthetic smile transformations, while incorporating digital technology into contemporary treatment planning. Her experience as an orthodontic patient during her postgraduate years also shaped her approach to patient education and understanding the questions and concerns people face during treatment.Since starting dental education content during the COVID-19 pandemic, Dr. Rachita has built an organic social media community of more than 31,000 followers, using digital platforms to make dental science simpler and more accessible. She also conducts courses, webinars and personal branding sessions for dentists. Her work in dental education has earned her the National Icon Award from the Indian Dental Association, and she was also nominated for Social Media Dentist of the Year 2026 at the Famdent Awards.Dr. Naresh Kumar: Advancing Implant Dentistry Through Innovation Dr. Naresh Kumar is a Hyderabad-based prosthodontist and implantologist with more than two decades of clinical experience, specialising in advanced implant dentistry, All-on-X rehabilitation, digital dentistry, and zygomatic implant procedures. As the founder of Vivasmilez Dental, he focuses on complex implant and full mouth rehabilitation cases, combining clinical expertise with evolving digital workflows.Beyond patient care, Dr. Kumar has contributed to dental education and professional development, having trained more than 500 dentists in advanced implant dentistry. Through training programmes, lectures and keynote sessions, he has worked to share his experience and expertise with fellow dental professionals, reflecting the growing role of technology and advanced techniques in modern implantology.Dr. Swati Bharti: Redefining Excellence in Cosmetic DentistryDr. Swati Bharti is a Manipal-trained dentist with more than 25 years of experience, with a clinical focus on root canal treatment, aesthetic and cosmetic dentistry. She is the founder and lead dentist of Rootz Dentz Dental Clinic in Andheri, Mumbai, where she has built an established practice serving more than 3,000 families. Her patient base includes business professionals, NRIs, international patients and a growing number of television personalities and professionals from Mumbai’s entertainment industry.Her work includes smile makeovers, veneers, clear aligners and root canal treatment, with an emphasis on natural-looking outcomes and individualised treatment planning. Dr. Bharti remains closely involved throughout the patient journey, from consultation and clinical planning to post-treatment care and follow-up. Her approach combines aesthetic sensitivity, clinical precision and clear communication, helping Rootz Dentz build long-standing relationships with patients across generations while maintaining a highly personalised approach to dental care.Dr. Shweta N. Lokhande: Championing Preventive and Sustainable Dentistry Dr. Shweta N. Lokhande is a dentist, lecturer, author, global health researcher, oral health educator and certified career counsellor whose work brings together clinical practice, education, public health and community impact. With expertise in global health and research, she advocates for preventive, accessible and sustainable healthcare. As teaching faculty in Community Medicine, she contributes to teaching, mentoring, research supervision, curriculum development, scientific publications and professional preceptorship. Her experience as a registered Dental Care Professional in the UK further informs her perspective on equitable, patient-centred care.Beyond academics and research, Dr. Lokhande promotes engaging, eco-conscious oral health education and community well-being. She also heads the Institutional Forum for Women Empowerment (IFFW), where she works to advance women’s education, confidence, leadership and financial independence. Her contributions have received national and international recognition. Across her varied roles, she continues to combine education, research and advocacy with a focus on creating practical, meaningful change at the grassroots level within healthcare and communities.ConclusionThe journeys of these dentists highlight how the profession is evolving beyond the conventional dental practice. stories.headline: What does a delayed US trade deal mean for India?
stories.title: What does a delayed US trade deal mean for India?
stories.summary: A delay in the India-US trade deal adds to the uncertainty that’s already weighing on industry but by itself does not represent a major shock to India’s GDP growth outlook, say economists.“The key issue is not simply the timing of the agreement, but whether the delay results in India facing a materially higher and more persistent tariff disadvantage relative to competing exporters,” says Rajani Sinha, chief economist at CareEdge Ratings.Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at Bank of Baroda, says the lack of a deal is a concern but the impact is hard to quantify.“Impact on exports will be there though not much on GDP as a lot of it is made up by service exports.”Indian goods shipments to the US currently face a 10 percent tariff, plus a most favoured nation (MFN) duty which varies across sectors.The 10 percent levy was imposed on India in July under Section 301 of the Trade Act, where the US cited concerns around forced labour.Also Read: India-US trade talks hit a plateau as FM flags tough road aheadThe rate is far below what Indian goods faced a year ago. Last year, India faced a 25 percent “reciprocal” tariff, which was raised to 50 percent after the US added another 25 percent over purchases of Russian oil.The US and India agreed on a framework for an interim deal on February 6, which cut the rate to 18 percent. article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (October 9, 2026) stood firm by its decision to ban the unauthorised use and circulation of livestreamed judicial proceedings on social media and digital platforms, saying “anything meant for public good” cannot be “exploited” commercially for personal gain.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant clarified that the explicit bar did not amount to a gag or restriction on viewing live-streamed proceedings or court reportage.
“Court proceedings are simply not meant for commercial exploitation.
Anything meant for public good should not be exploited for money,” the Chief Justice said.

Justice Joymalya Bagchi, on the Bench, pointed out that court proceedings are live-streamed 24x7 in the United Kingdom and the United States, but the access was subject to strict guidelines against commercialisation.
“The first bar imposed by the Bar Council of India is that a lawyer will not canvas for professional gains.
Today, uploading and promotion for personal gain is being done, and it is very serious.
We notice that lawyers upload and canvas these videos for their own promotional purposes… Such actions are completely adverse to advocacy and the legal profession,” Justice Bagchi said.
The court gave the parties and other stakeholders time to file pleadings, along with suggestions for guidelines against commercialisation of live-streamed proceedings.
The Supreme Court had clarified on July 31 that recognised news outlets would be able to continue reporting on court proceedings without “utilising” audio and video clippings of judicial hearings.

On July 24, the court had passed an interim direction prohibiting extraction, dissemination, monetisation, posting, re-posting, uploading, transmitting, modification, storing, or hosting of the audio-video recording(s) of judicial proceedings on social media or any other digital platforms without prior permission of the Secretary General of the Supreme Court or the Registrars General of the jurisdictional High Courts.

An application filed by two activists, Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, represented by advocates Prashant Bhushan and Cheryl D’souza, had criticised the July 24 order as a reversal of the ‘principle of open justice’ upheld by the apex court itself in a plethora of judgments.

stories.title: SC seeks response of States, UTs on plea alleging prolonged vacancies in power regulatory bodies
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 9: The Supreme Court on Friday sought a response from 15 states and the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh on a PIL filed by NGO Energy Watchdog seeking directions to ensure that their state electricity regulatory commissions are properly constituted under the law. The bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice on the PIL filed by the NGO through lawyer Pranav Sachdeva. The petitioner has sought the apex court's directions directing the states and UTs to take all steps to comply with the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003, and with the directions of the apex court in a verdict of April 2018 regarding composition of State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs). The plea said there were several "statutory infractions", such as prolonged vacancies in the offices of chairperson and members and the complete absence of a person of law on the Commission, across 230 SERCs in the 15 states and the UTs. In the 2018 ruling, the Supreme Court held that SERCs have the "trappings of the court" and must have a suitably qualified person of law as a member, the plea said. It said the commissions across several states, including West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland, continue to lack a person of law despite this ruling. The plea said in Tamil Nadu, all three offices are vacant, while in Andhra Pradesh, the chairperson and member (technical) posts are vacant, and the Commission functions with a sole member (finance). It said that in West Bengal, only the chairperson's office has been created, and the incumbent does not have the required legal background. The plea said the failure "strikes at consumers' access to justice" under Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution and, without the mandated person of law, consumers cannot get lawful adjudication of complaints under the Electricity Act. "Consumers' access to that remedy cannot be made dependent upon indefinite executive inaction," the plea said. It sought directions to the states of West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Kerala, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Manipur, Nagaland, Mizoram and Sikkim, and to the UTs of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, directing the authorities concerned to file a reply disclosing the steps taken to ensure that their SERCs had been constituted in compliance with the Electricity Act provisions.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (October 9, 2026) pulled up the Keralam government for its failure to inform the court of the measures taken to protect Uttoly Raman, the State’s tallest captive elephant, after the tusker’s custody was handed over to the government in June.
The court directed the authorities to place the latest medical examination report of the elephant, which has been at the centre of a long-running ownership dispute, before it on October 12.

A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu asked why these details had not been disclosed in the State’s affidavit and why the court had been kept in the dark about the steps taken to ensure the animal’s welfare.
The State’s counsel informed the Bench that there had been a delay in taking custody of the elephant from its caretaker, Krishnankutty, due to the Assembly elections in Kerala.
Expressing serious reservations over the submission, Justice Datta remarked, “It is a wonderful argument to make.
So, the Supreme Court order is not to be complied with all these months because there were elections?”
The Bench also sought to know when the transfer of custody had eventually taken place and why the fact had not been mentioned in the State’s affidavit.
The court further directed the State to ensure that the former caretaker, who has been accused of “commercially exploiting” the elephant, is not allowed to touch the animal.
The court had earlier pulled up the caretaker over his treatment of the elephant.
“The only love and affection you have for the elephant is for the love of money.

You have commercially exploited the elephant,” the Bench had told Mr. Krishnankutty, who was found guilty of contempt in June for violating an undertaking that the animal would not be used for commercial or temple activities.
The Bench then turned to the elephant’s present condition, seeking details of the medical care provided to it since the June order.

The Supreme Court today directed Sir Ganga Ram Hospital in Delhi to provide all necessary treatment, regardless of cost, to an acid attack survivor admitted there after sustaining damage to both her eyes.
A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana passed the order when the matter was mentioned around 4 PM by a woman appearing in-person on behalf of the survivor.
The woman informed the Court that the acid attack survivor was currently in Ganga Ram Hospital but was being threatened with discharge.
She alleged that the hospital was claiming that it was not "specialized" in the required treatment.
The woman further claimed that Apollo Hospital was also consulted, but it declined to take in the survivor.
It was further submitted that the survivor did not wish to go to a government hospital.
The woman highlighted that vide its orders, the Supreme Court has given acid attack survivors the right to avail treatment in any private hospital of their choice.
"Ganga Ram mei hai, toh wahin rakhte hain (if she is in Ganga Ram, then let her be there only)", the CJI responded.
The woman in-person agreed, while submitting that if at all the survivor is to be transferred out of Ganga Ram hospital, she should be allowed treatment in Apollo Hospital.

Ultimately, the Court directed the management of Sir Ganga Ram hospital to take in the survivor as an indoor patient and provide all facilities, including medicines and plastic surgery, as and when required, irrespective of the cost to be incurred on the treatment.

As against allegation of the hospital forcing the survivor to leave the hospital, the Court added that the hospital shall not discharge her until doctors certify that she is fit for discharge and will require only outdoor treatment.

stories.title: India’s logistics sector eyes $600 billion by 2031-32; cost pegged at 8% of GDP: DPIIT official

article_sentences: India’s logistics sector is expected to double in size to $600 billion by 2031-32 from around $300 billion currently, driven by infrastructure development, policy reforms and improved connectivity, said Subhash Chandra Karol, Director, Logistics Division, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).
Logistics contributed more than 13 per cent to India’s GDP and played a critical role in supporting manufacturing growth.

The two sectors were complementary, making efficient logistics infrastructure essential to strengthening the country’s manufacturing ecosystem, he said while addressing at PRISM 2026 – Powering Recognition: India’s Skill Movement, hosted by the Logistics Sector Skill Council (LSC) in association with National Skill Development Council on Friday.
A study conducted by DPIIT in 2025 estimated India’s logistics costs at around 8 per cent of GDP, challenging the earlier perception that they accounted for 13-14 per cent.
The reduction reflects the impact of government reforms and efforts to improve logistics efficiency, although the official noted that comparable estimates had not been available earlier.
India has also improved its position in the Logistics Performance Index (LPI), moving from 46th in 2018 to 30th.
The government aims to bring the country into the top 25 within the next five years, said Karol.
Infrastructure connectivity remains central to improving logistics efficiency, with better links needed between manufacturing hubs, consumption centres and last-mile destinations.
The government launched PM Gati Shakti in 2021 as a digital platform to coordinate infrastructure planning across ministries.

The platform helps identify gaps in connectivity, locate underserved areas and anticipate implementation hurdles, including forest areas and restricted zones, before projects reach the execution stage.
This enables authorities to plan clearances in advance and reduce delays during implementation, the official said.
The pace of road construction has increased from around 5-6 km a day to more than 15 km a day on average, according to the official.

General Subramani also put forth three asks from the industry on volume, scale, and speed and assured that the relationship between defence forces and the companies is now that of an “industry partner” and not as a vendor.

Speaking at “Annual Session and Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers (SIDM) Champions Award 2026”, the CDS said, “We will give a clear demand signal of over 5 to 7 years and also technology capability signals which have already been done through prospective development programmes.
In order to become better partners, come up with an innovative product that we are compelled to buy or create demand for that, instead of finger pointing over lack of business.”
The General was speaking on one of the sessions on jointness, multi-domain integration and national deterrence, which was moderated by Baba Kalyani, industry veteran and founder president of SIDM.
The CDS stated that long range missiles are the need of the hour and that they are working with the industry to get home grown products.
“We would like to have a missile that fires till 500 km to 600 km first and range can be increased further later,” he put forth the demand.
But, he added a caveat - built it at a cost of less than ₹5 crore so that it’s affordable.
“If you come to us, we will ensure that the industry gets adequate orders.
We require cruise missiles, we require multiple rocket launchers.
Pinaka has a range of 70-80 kms, but today we want to have an extended version of 300-400 kms.

Similarly increase the range of artillery gun ammunition because we cannot change the barrels,” he said, giving a development-cum-manufacturing roadmap to the gathering of representatives of industry, MSMEs and start-ups.

The bench also demanded an updated medical report on the pachyderm's health.

Hearing the matter, a bench comprising Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu was told by counsel that the elephant remained with his private caretaker because the animal had entered musth—a natural biological phase characterised by extremely high testosterone levels—making relocation unsafe.
Defending his physical custody, the caretaker assured the apex court that the animal was being maintained with utmost affection and attention.
"Love, care and for the purpose of earning money by defying the Supreme Court's restraint orders.

"In the next date of hearing, the state shall faithfully and honestly comply with the court's order dated June 9, 2026, in so far as the upkeep of the elephant is concerned."
The legal battle stems from a contempt petition moved by Jayakrishna Menon.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice On Plea To Fill Vacancies In Electricity Regulatory Commissions In 15 States, J&K
stories.title: Supreme Court Issues Notice On Plea To Fill Vacancies In Electricity Regulatory Commissions In 15 States, J&K
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (October 9) issued notice on a PIL filed by NGO Energy Watchdog over prolonged vacancies and absence of legally qualified members in State Electricity Regulatory Commissions of 15 States and Jammu and Kashmir.
A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana issued notice.
The plea contends that the prolonged vacancies amount to violation of Article 21 of the Constitution, the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Supreme Court's 2018 judgment in State of Gujarat.
Utility Users' Welfare Association.
“The continuing failure to provide a lawfully constituted Commission strikes at consumers' access to justice under Articles 14 and 21.

In the absence of the mandated person of law, consumers cannot obtain lawful adjudication of complaints invoking Section 142 of the Electricity Act against distribution licensees where the statutory conditions for such proceedings are fulfilled.
Consumers' access to that remedy cannot be made dependent upon indefinite executive inaction in filling the offices of the very institution entrusted with enforcing the law.
In Tamil Nadu, the complete absence of Members disables both adjudicatory and regulatory functioning”, the plea contends.

The petition seeks directions to the concerned State Governments and authorities to ensure that the Commissions are constituted as per Sections 82, 84 and 85 of the Electricity Act and the 2018 judgment.

In that case, the Court held that a suitably qualified person of law must be a member of a State Electricity Regulatory Commission and every bench exercising adjudicatory functions must include such a member.

The petition has been filed against West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Kerala, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Sikkim, Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland, and the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, which is served by the Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission for Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.

The petition contends that the vacancies and deficiencies in the composition of these Commissions affect their ability to discharge regulatory and adjudicatory functions and undermine electricity consumers' access to effective legal remedies.

He also told the caretaker: "Love, care and for the purpose of earning money by defying the Supreme Court's restraint orders.
We quite understand what love and affection is.
We are not going to hear you."

stories.headline: Telangana CM Revanth to review El Nino impact, drought conditions on October 12
stories.title: Telangana CM Revanth to review El Nino impact, drought conditions on October 12
stories.summary: The action plan prepared by Telangana Cabinet sub-committee on drought mitigation, along with relief measures likely to be examined
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy will hold a special meeting with Ministers on October 12 to review the impact of El Nino and the prevailing rainfall deficit in Telangana, with a focus on relief measures for farmers and steps to address emerging water and power requirements.

The meeting is expected to take stock of conditions in areas that have received insufficient rainfall, the difficulties faced by farmers and the immediate interventions required to mitigate the impact of the dry spell.
Agriculture, irrigation, drinking water supply and the rising demand for electricity will be among the key issues on the agenda.
The move comes after an extensive discussion on the rainfall deficit at the recent State Cabinet meeting.
Telangana has recorded 17% less rainfall than normal, with drought-like conditions prevailing in nearly 235 mandals, according to official estimates cited by the government.
The State government has already adopted a resolution in the Legislative Assembly urging the Centre to declare drought-affected mandals and extend adequate financial assistance.
It has also sought a special package of Rs.
20,000 crore to help the State tackle the impact of the deficient rainfall.

The meeting on Tuesday is likely to examine the action plan prepared by the Cabinet sub-committee on drought mitigation, along with relief measures that need to be taken up in rainfall-deficient areas.
Suggestions emerging from political parties, consultations with farmers’ organisations and inputs from experts in various sectors are also expected to figure in the discussions.
